capabilities.heading: Bureau provides one dimension
capabilities.lead: A bureau score reports what a borrower did with another institution's capital, months ago. It does not know the phone number was registered last month, that the SMS inbox holds 12 bounce notifications, or that the same device filed four other applications this week.
hero.deck: Bureau scores are backward-looking by design and silent on 300 million Indians with no credit history. The signals that predict default, first-payment failure and over-leveraging exist at the moment of application — in the device, the digital footprint, the SMS inbox and the behavioural session. Shruhani captures them, calibrates them to your own portfolio, and delivers a view that's independent of the bureau score.

scenarios.heading: Five places bureau alone leaves the decision short
scenarios.sub: For each: the challenge, why current systems fail, how Shruhani addresses it — and what it measured on a production portfolio.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[0].description: 300 million Indians carry no bureau score. An application from this segment returns no data, and the underwriting model defaults to decline. The borrower is not necessarily high-risk; the scoring infrastructure is simply unable to evaluate them.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[0].title: The challenge
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[1].description: Bureau-dependent scorecards need a minimum credit history to produce a score. Without one, no score is generated and no decision is possible. The model treats absence of data as presence of risk.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[1].title: Why current systems fail
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[2].description: Shruhani builds a credit-relevant profile from alternate data: footprint depth across 100+ platforms, SMS-derived salary regularity and bounce patterns, device price band, location affluence, and application-portfolio analysis — all independent of bureau.
scenarios.tabs[0].cards[2].title: How Shruhani addresses it
scenarios.tabs[0].label: NTC & thin-file
scenarios.tabs[0].proofBody: uplift in monthly disbursals with no corresponding increase in default rates.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[0].description: A first-payment default is the earliest confirmation that the origination decision was wrong — and by then the money is out the door. The signals that would have predicted it were available at application, but never entered the credit decision.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[0].title: The challenge
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[1].description: Bureau scores reflect historical repayment, not current financial condition. A borrower whose salary credits have stopped, who has 12 EMI bounces in 60 days and has registered on 8 lending apps this month stays invisible to a backward-looking score.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[1].title: Why current systems fail
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[2].description: SMS Parser captures real-time financial behaviour at application: salary regularity, bounce patterns, UPI velocity, recent disbursals. Combined with device and footprint signals, Shruhani scores FPD risk before disbursal — months before bureau would surface it.
scenarios.tabs[1].cards[2].title: How Shruhani addresses it
scenarios.tabs[1].label: First-payment default
scenarios.tabs[1].proofBody: of NPAs concentrated in the riskiest 5% of scored applicants.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[0].description: A borrower takes on multiple obligations across lenders within days. Each lender sees only its own application. Bureau reporting lags two to three months, so by the time the pattern is visible several lenders have already disbursed to the same over-leveraged individual.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[0].title: The challenge
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[1].description: Reporting cycles create a structural blind spot. A loan disbursed on Monday does not appear in a bureau pull on Wednesday. Three lenders can disburse within a week, each unaware of the others.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[1].title: Why current systems fail
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[2].description: SMS Parser identifies disbursal and EMI obligation messages in real time; Digital Footprint detects presence across multiple lending platforms. Together they surface the stacking pattern at the next application, not three months later.
scenarios.tabs[2].cards[2].title: How Shruhani addresses it
scenarios.tabs[2].label: Loan stacking
scenarios.tabs[2].proofBody: Information Value for presence on 5+ lending platforms — a strong standalone predictor of credit stress.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[0].description: Borrowers already on the book were assessed at origination. Their risk has since moved: some are over-leveraged, some have lost income, some were marginal approvals the model got wrong. The risk sits inside the portfolio, undetected until delinquency.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[0].title: The challenge
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[1].description: Post-disbursal monitoring depends on bureau refreshes and payment history — both lagging indicators. Early warnings such as behavioural drift, device changes and new stacking live outside the systems watching the book.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[1].title: Why current systems fail
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[2].description: Shruhani scores an existing portfolio retroactively. Historical applicant data (phone, email, device, outcome labels) runs through the signal modules and returns a risk classification for every borrower, surfacing concentrations invisible at origination.
scenarios.tabs[3].cards[2].title: How Shruhani addresses it
scenarios.tabs[3].label: Portfolio risk scoring
scenarios.tabs[3].proofBody: of an already-approved portfolio reclassified as elevated-risk when scored retroactively.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[0].description: Internal credit models hit diminishing returns once the feature set is exhausted. Bureau-derived variables are optimised to their practical limit; the scorecard is stable but no longer improving. Further lift needs orthogonal data, not more tuning.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[0].title: The challenge
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[1].description: Bureau supplies the same feature set to every institution in the market, so differentiation through it is structurally constrained. Building proprietary alternate-data pipelines takes years of investment and ongoing maintenance.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[1].title: Why current systems fail
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[2].description: Shruhani delivers 500+ raw features per applicant, consumable directly into an existing scorecard or BRE: WhatsApp absence (IV 0.319), lending app count (IV 0.230), phone vintage, email depth, device price band, location affluence — orthogonal lift with no rebuild.
scenarios.tabs[4].cards[2].title: How Shruhani addresses it
scenarios.tabs[4].label: Scorecard enhancement
scenarios.tabs[4].proofBody: fraud capture ratio using phone and email data alone, with alternate features outperforming most bureau features on NTC.

split.body:
Indian digital lending is growing at 30%+ CAGR, and the borrowers driving that growth are disproportionately new-to-credit, thin-file, or gig-economy workers with no bureau history. For these segments the traditional infrastructure returns no score — and the absence of a score is treated as grounds for decline.
The cost extends beyond the individual rejection. It is market share conceded to institutions that have found alternative means to assess them. Meanwhile the risks bureau does track are months stale: a borrower who has taken on three new obligations this week still reflects last month's score. The gap between reported data and actual behaviour widens with every reporting cycle.
